sentences.text: Facts of the present case are that Akarshan Bhardwaj and the complaint were married on 13.03.2019 and there is one issue from their wedlock.

On 18.08.2023 when the complainant was staying in her parental house, she lodged the FIR against the present applicants making allegations that after marriage there was a demand of gold ornaments and the applicants also pressurized the complainant to get share of the property from her parents.
Thereafter, Rs. 1,00,000/- was deposited by her parents in her bank account.
On such complaint police registered the FIR for the offence as stated above.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the present applicants have not committed any offence, they are innocent and a false complaint has been registered after five years of marriage.
He would further submit that there are general and omnibus allegations against the applicants.

Thus, he would pray for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicants.
5.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State would oppose the bail applications.

Mr.
Chitendra Singh would submit that there are serious allegations against the present applicants with regard to demand of dowry and cruelty, therefore, the applications deserve to be rejected.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

7. From the perusal of the case diary it appears that on 18.08.2023 the FIR was registered against the present applicants for commission of an offence punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of the IPC.
From a perusal of the FIR it is apparent that there are general and omnibus allegations with regard to demand of dowry.

Taking into consideration the fact that there is one issue from the marriage of applicant Akarshan Bhardwaj and the complainant and the FIR has been registered after about five years of marriage, I am inclined to allow both these applications.
8.
Accordingly, both the anticipatory bail applications filed under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. are allowed.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, both the anticipatory bail applications filed under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. are allowed.
It is directed that in the event of each of the applicants executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- to the satisfaction of the concerned arresting officer, they shall be released on bail,
on following conditions:-
(i) that they shall make themselves available for interrogation before the investigating officer as and when required;
(ii) that they shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
(iii) that they shall not act, in any manner, which will be prejudicial to fair and expeditious trial; and (iv) that they shall appear before the trial Court on each and every date given to them by the said Court till disposal of the trial.
The observations made in the course of this order are only for considering the case of the applicants for grant of anticipatory bail.
The concerned trial Court shall not be influenced or bound by any observations made hereinabove.
